meta.title: URL Abuse × Lookyloo
meta.description: Planned architecture: URL Abuse is an API broker for URLs (rebuilt backend, web view, public API and incoming data stream kept): it forwards each URL to the providers and returns their answers; Lookyloo is one provider called through PyLookyloo; other providers come later. Arrows show the calls and the data flows.

nodes.label: URL Abuse
nodes.description: URL Abuse (CIRCL): an API broker for URLs. It receives a URL, forwards it to the providers and returns their answers through one API. No analysis of its own: the logic stays in the providers.

nodes.description: The URL Abuse backend is rewritten as a broker: one call per provider through its client library (PyLookyloo, ...), answers returned as they are, side by side. No analysis logic of its own.

nodes.label: Lookyloo
nodes.description: Lookyloo is one provider among others: captures the URL in a real browser (redirects, resources, screenshot, tree, indexes). Nothing URL Abuse specific is added to Lookyloo.

nodes.label:
Decisions

• URL Abuse is only an API broker for URLs: it forwards to the providers and returns their answers.
• One implementation: the analysis lives in the providers (Lookyloo...), nothing is duplicated in URL Abuse.
• Lookyloo stays a provider like any other, called with PyLookyloo (which has all the calls); no URL Abuse view or logic inside Lookyloo.
• The URL Abuse API and the incoming data stream are kept for compatibility.
• Other providers (MISP modules, pivot services) are added later in the same way.
